key_insight: Online Reasoning Calibration (ORCA) uses test-time training plus conformal prediction to calibrate LLM sampling on the fly, achieving reliable reasoning accuracy without expensive brute-force scaling. This lets models stop or adapt sampling based on calibrated confidence, saving compute while preserving performance.
problem_solved: Addresses miscalibration in post-trained LLMs and in common sampling strategies that force practitioners to rely on costly test-time scaling (massive sampling or larger models) to reach state-of-the-art reasoning performance.
method: Apply conformal prediction to sampled reasoning chains to produce calibrated confidence bounds for each output.
Perform lightweight test-time training on unlabeled test instances to adapt the model/sampling distribution and improve calibration online.
Use calibrated confidences to control sampling: stop early, resample adaptively, or accept/reject outputs to meet accuracy or cost targets.
impact: ORCA enables practitioners to get high-confidence reasoning results with far less compute by turning calibration into an actionable, online control signal—improving reliability, efficiency, and generalization across tasks and model sizes.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: input → test-time training adapter → sampling loop → conformal calibrator → accept/reject or resample decision
Bar chart: compute cost (tokens/samples) vs. accuracy comparing baseline heavy sampling, larger-model scaling, and ORCA
Calibration plot: predicted confidence vs. empirical accuracy showing improved calibration after ORCA
Icon set: clock/energy (compute savings), shield (reliability), gears (online adaptation)
paper_title: Online Reasoning Calibration: Test-Time Training Enables Generalizable Conformal LLM Reasoning
paper_authors: Cai Zhou, Zekai Wang, Menghua Wu, Qianyu Julie Zhu, Flora C. Shi
